# Measurement

Two things, both small: a weekly record of how Caliper compares with react-docgen-typescript (RDT) and react-docgen on five public repos, and `just bench` for a change that touches the resolver. Nothing here blocks a pull request.

## Weekly record

`.github/workflows/weekly.yml` runs on Mondays and by hand. `scripts/corpora.py` fetches each repo at a pinned commit and installs its dependencies with its own package manager and lockfile (lifecycle scripts off, caches under `.corpora/`, gitignored), then removes tests, stories, demos and the `dist/` and `build/` directories from the source directory so every tool reads the same files. `scripts/weekly.py` runs the tools.

Declaration files are kept. Until 2026-11 the fetch also deleted every `.d.ts`, which removed a corpus's own type packages: React Spectrum declares `@react-types/shared` in `packages/@react-types/shared/src/*.d.ts` and its components import from it. With those files gone, 20 props that reach a component through `Pick` of a name declared there were lost; on unmodified main with the files restored, Caliper reports 20 of 20. Generated declarations sit in `dist/` and `build/`, which are still removed. A fetched corpus records a prune version in its marker (`PRUNE_VERSION` in `scripts/corpora.py`), so one pruned under the older rule is fetched again on the next `setup`; `--sparse` never pruned and already kept declaration files. The first weekly run after this change moves Caliper's and RDT's numbers on every corpus whose source tree holds `.d.ts` files (React Spectrum has 67 under `packages/`).

| Corpus | Repository | Commit | Source directory | Install |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mantine | `mantinedev/mantine` | `e47e45af06427b3b2497100c2b849935c23af30d` | `packages/@mantine/core/src` | yarn, immutable |
| chakra | `chakra-ui/chakra-ui` | `fa9696f328ea5a0df8685c6d8460edbd779b63b9` | `packages/react/src` | pnpm, frozen |
| shadcn | `shadcn-ui/ui` | `ba1503c64472b82256d9de95e2e62c5901a38e8b` | `apps/v4` | pnpm, frozen |
| antd | `ant-design/ant-design` | `ba7ccbaa7b4b58ac1ff8e6fe2e78dfa10bfb5538` | `components` | npm, no lockfile (the repo commits none) |
| spectrum | `adobe/react-spectrum` | `797762ed3526ea12f089e321bd3891066affad70` | `packages` | yarn, immutable |

It records, per corpus and tool, the wall time and peak RSS of one whole run (process start and Node start included), and the size of Caliper's canonical JSON. Caliper runs with `--load-dependencies` and `--no-checker`; its time is the median of five runs. Since ADR 0026's S8 the checker answers by default, so the record (time, memory, recall and the oracle's verdicts) is the structural resolver's, the fallback, and its budgets (2 s, 600 MiB) are that resolver's: the checker's whole-project run takes seconds on a large program (`docs/gate-measurements.md`, "The checker is the default"). Recording the checker weekly needs budgets of its own first. RDT and react-docgen run once each.

Each run's peak RSS is that process's own. `scripts/corpora.py` starts every measured command through a small helper that forks it and reads its `wait4` usage. Reading it straight from the weekly script gave one number for every run after the largest: on Linux a child's `ru_maxrss` starts at the highest RSS its parent ever had, and the script's own peak (it holds RDT's output for a large corpus) became every later tool's "peak". The first weekly record shows 1,593 MiB for all three tools on shadcn, antd and spectrum, which is that. `scripts/test_weekly.py` checks that a large parent no longer leaks in.

### The reference

Recall is measured against RDT's output, cleaned in two steps. Both are by what RDT reports, never by library or name lists, and `weekly.json` keeps their counts (`reference` per corpus) so a change in either is visible.

| Step | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Not components, left out | More than half of the props are declared in TypeScript's own `lib.*.d.ts` (the parameter is a `string`, a `Request`, a function: `GET`, `loadHighlighter`, `convertLegacyProps`). The name is a hook's (`use` and a capital). The only props are a `value` (and `children`) declared by `@types/react`, which is a context's Provider (`FormContext`). The name starts lowercase, is not the file's or directory's name (RDT names a default export after those) and no prop comes from `@types/react`, so it is no JSX tag and takes no tag's attributes (`genLinkStyle`, `generateMetadata`). Every prop is a `Promise<...>`, which a router hands over (`page`). |
| Repeats, counted once | RDT lists one component under each file that re-exports it, and names a default export after the file or directory (antd's `col/index.tsx` default-exports `Col` from `../grid` and RDT reports `col` there; Caliper reports the defining file). An entry that Caliper does not report in its own file pairs by evidence: where the default export, or the named export, of RDT's file is defined (followed through `export default X`, `import`, `export { X } from` and `export { default as X }`), or else the file that declares its props when Caliper reports a component of that name there. The same evidence works inside one file: a default export that is another name (`const InternalButton = ...; export default InternalButton`, which RDT calls `button`), or the component whose `displayName` RDT reports. Both are guarded: the RDT name must be the file's or directory's own, so a member such as `Form.List` is never paired with `Form`, and a Caliper key that another RDT entry matches exactly is never a target. A call around the name (`memo(Foo)`, `React.forwardRef(Foo)`, `Object.assign(Foo, { Item })`), a type assertion (`Foo as T`, `Foo satisfies T`, `Foo!`) and a chain of local aliases (`const A = memo(B)`) lead to the declaration; Caliper's `displayName` for it counts as its name. Entries that pair with the same Caliper component are one reference item. |

The record shows, per corpus: RDT's entries with props, how many are not components, how many repeats were merged, the reference size, how many match in the same file, how many are paired (by default export, default alias, `displayName`, named export or declaration) and how many stay unpaired. `weekly.json` also records the `reference_version`: the rules above are version 2 (a record without it is version 1), and recall is not compared with a record made under other rules, so a change to them cannot read as a regression or hide one. Pairing needs the names to agree: the component the export resolves to must have the name Caliper reports, so an entry never pairs with an unrelated component just because it is the only one in its file. When several RDT entries pair to one component, the reference takes the props of the entry in the component's own file, else the union of the repeats'. An unpaired item is a component Caliper does not report where RDT does, and it stays in the denominator.

The 2026-10-31 effect on the pinned corpora, Caliper's component recall (own and `@types/react` props are unchanged by the exclusions and move only a little with the pairing):

| Corpus | Reference before |                                           After | Components before | After |
| ------ | ---------------: | ----------------------------------------------: | ----------------: | ----: |
| shadcn |             1594 |                   1573 (21 left out, 0 repeats) |             95.2% | 96.5% |
| antd   |              258 | 203 (43 left out, 12 repeats merged, 12 paired) |             64.0% | 81.3% |

Exclusions alone give 76.7% on antd, pairing alone 68.3%.

The 2026-11-02 pairing (same-file default aliases, `displayName`, wrappers, assertions, alias chains), replayed on the pinned commits with RDT's output and Caliper's at that day's `main`:

| Corpus | Reference before | After | Components before |        After |
| ------ | ---------------: | ----: | ----------------: | -----------: |
| shadcn |             1573 |  1573 |      1518 (96.5%) | 1518 (96.5%) |
| antd   |              207 |   202 |       165 (79.7%) |  186 (92.1%) |

Each corpus entry's `reference.unmatched` says why the items Caliper reports nowhere are missing: `by_cause` counts them and `listed` names the first 15 of each cause as `file: name`. The cause is what the item's file shows, so it says where to look, not what is wrong:

| Cause | The file shows |
| --- | --- |
| `compound_member` | An assignment to a member of another component (`Form.List = List`). |
| `object_member` | The name as a function-valued key of an object literal (`logo: () => ...`). |
| `dependency` | An alias of something a package exports (`const Tooltip = Recharts.Tooltip`), or an export that ends in a package. |
| `call_result` | A value a call builds (`createIcon(...)`, `generateCalendar(...)`). |
| `file_with_other_components`, `file_without_components` | A declaration Caliper does not report, in a file where it reports others, or none. |

The 14 antd items still unpaired in the weekly run of 2026-11-06 (16 when this was first written) are not pairing cases: the date picker and calendar families (built by factory functions), `Parent.Member` entries Caliper reports under the parent (`Form.List`, `Mentions.Option`, `TreeSelect.TreeNode`), and helpers RDT lists as components (`confirm`, `dropIndicator`). shadcn has no re-export of this kind in the pinned commit, so nothing pairs there; its unpaired items are `Icons.logo`-style object members, aliases such as `const ComboboxRoot = Primitive.Root` and factory results, which Caliper does not detect.

## Weekly record

`.github/workflows/weekly.yml` runs on Mondays and by hand. `scripts/corpora.py` fetches each repo at a pinned commit and installs its dependencies with its own package manager and lockfile (lifecycle scripts off, caches under `.corpora/`, gitignored), then removes tests, stories, demos and the `dist/` and `build/` directories from the source directory so every tool reads the same files. `scripts/weekly.py` runs the tools.

Declaration files are kept. Until 2026-11 the fetch also deleted every `.d.ts`, which removed a corpus's own type packages: React Spectrum declares `@react-types/shared` in `packages/@react-types/shared/src/*.d.ts` and its components import from it. With those files gone, 20 props that reach a component through `Pick` of a name declared there were lost; on unmodified main with the files restored, Caliper reports 20 of 20. Generated declarations sit in `dist/` and `build/`, which are still removed. A fetched corpus records a prune version in its marker (`PRUNE_VERSION` in `scripts/corpora.py`), so one pruned under the older rule is fetched again on the next `setup`; `--sparse` never pruned and already kept declaration files. The first weekly run after this change moves Caliper's and RDT's numbers on every corpus whose source tree holds `.d.ts` files (React Spectrum has 67 under `packages/`).

| Corpus | Repository | Commit | Source directory | Install |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mantine | `mantinedev/mantine` | `e47e45af06427b3b2497100c2b849935c23af30d` | `packages/@mantine/core/src` | yarn, immutable |
| chakra | `chakra-ui/chakra-ui` | `fa9696f328ea5a0df8685c6d8460edbd779b63b9` | `packages/react/src` | pnpm, frozen |
| shadcn | `shadcn-ui/ui` | `ba1503c64472b82256d9de95e2e62c5901a38e8b` | `apps/v4` | pnpm, frozen |
| antd | `ant-design/ant-design` | `ba7ccbaa7b4b58ac1ff8e6fe2e78dfa10bfb5538` | `components` | npm, no lockfile (the repo commits none) |
| spectrum | `adobe/react-spectrum` | `797762ed3526ea12f089e321bd3891066affad70` | `packages` | yarn, immutable |

It records, per corpus and tool, the wall time and peak RSS of one whole run (process start and Node start included), and the size of Caliper's canonical JSON. Caliper runs with `--load-dependencies` and `--no-checker`; its time is the median of five runs. Since ADR 0026's S8 the checker answers by default, so the record (time, memory, recall and the oracle's verdicts) is the structural resolver's, the fallback, and its budgets (2 s, 600 MiB) are that resolver's: the checker's whole-project run takes seconds on a large program (`docs/gate-measurements.md`, "The checker is the default"). Recording the checker weekly needs budgets of its own first. RDT and react-docgen run once each.

Each run's peak RSS is that process's own. `scripts/corpora.py` starts every measured command through a small helper that forks it and reads its `wait4` usage. Reading it straight from the weekly script gave one number for every run after the largest: on Linux a child's `ru_maxrss` starts at the highest RSS its parent ever had, and the script's own peak (it holds RDT's output for a large corpus) became every later tool's "peak". The first weekly record shows 1,593 MiB for all three tools on shadcn, antd and spectrum, which is that. `scripts/test_weekly.py` checks that a large parent no longer leaks in.

### The reference

Recall is measured against RDT's output, cleaned in two steps. Both are by what RDT reports, never by library or name lists, and `weekly.json` keeps their counts (`reference` per corpus) so a change in either is visible.

| Step | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Not components, left out | More than half of the props are declared in TypeScript's own `lib.*.d.ts` (the parameter is a `string`, a `Request`, a function: `GET`, `loadHighlighter`, `convertLegacyProps`). The name is a hook's (`use` and a capital). The only props are a `value` (and `children`) declared by `@types/react`, which is a context's Provider (`FormContext`). The name starts lowercase, is not the file's or directory's name (RDT names a default export after those) and no prop comes from `@types/react`, so it is no JSX tag and takes no tag's attributes (`genLinkStyle`, `generateMetadata`). Every prop is a `Promise<...>`, which a router hands over (`page`). |
| Repeats, counted once | RDT lists one component under each file that re-exports it, and names a default export after the file or directory (antd's `col/index.tsx` default-exports `Col` from `../grid` and RDT reports `col` there; Caliper reports the defining file). An entry that Caliper does not report in its own file pairs by evidence: where the default export, or the named export, of RDT's file is defined (followed through `export default X`, `import`, `export { X } from` and `export { default as X }`), or else the file that declares its props when Caliper reports a component of that name there. The same evidence works inside one file: a default export that is another name (`const InternalButton = ...; export default InternalButton`, which RDT calls `button`), or the component whose `displayName` RDT reports. Both are guarded: the RDT name must be the file's or directory's own, so a member such as `Form.List` is never paired with `Form`, and a Caliper key that another RDT entry matches exactly is never a target. A call around the name (`memo(Foo)`, `React.forwardRef(Foo)`, `Object.assign(Foo, { Item })`), a type assertion (`Foo as T`, `Foo satisfies T`, `Foo!`) and a chain of local aliases (`const A = memo(B)`) lead to the declaration; Caliper's `displayName` for it counts as its name. Entries that pair with the same Caliper component are one reference item. |

The record shows, per corpus: RDT's entries with props, how many are not components, how many repeats were merged, the reference size, how many match in the same file, how many are paired (by default export, default alias, `displayName`, named export or declaration) and how many stay unpaired. `weekly.json` also records the `reference_version`: the rules above are version 2 (a record without it is version 1), and recall is not compared with a record made under other rules, so a change to them cannot read as a regression or hide one. Pairing needs the names to agree: the component the export resolves to must have the name Caliper reports, so an entry never pairs with an unrelated component just because it is the only one in its file. When several RDT entries pair to one component, the reference takes the props of the entry in the component's own file, else the union of the repeats'. An unpaired item is a component Caliper does not report where RDT does, and it stays in the denominator.

The 2026-10-31 effect on the pinned corpora, Caliper's component recall (own and `@types/react` props are unchanged by the exclusions and move only a little with the pairing):

| Corpus | Reference before |                                           After | Components before | After |
| ------ | ---------------: | ----------------------------------------------: | ----------------: | ----: |
| shadcn |             1594 |                   1573 (21 left out, 0 repeats) |             95.2% | 96.5% |
| antd   |              258 | 203 (43 left out, 12 repeats merged, 12 paired) |             64.0% | 81.3% |

Exclusions alone give 76.7% on antd, pairing alone 68.3%.

The 2026-11-02 pairing (same-file default aliases, `displayName`, wrappers, assertions, alias chains), replayed on the pinned commits with RDT's output and Caliper's at that day's `main`:

| Corpus | Reference before | After | Components before |        After |
| ------ | ---------------: | ----: | ----------------: | -----------: |
| shadcn |             1573 |  1573 |      1518 (96.5%) | 1518 (96.5%) |
| antd   |              207 |   202 |       165 (79.7%) |  186 (92.1%) |

Each corpus entry's `reference.unmatched` says why the items Caliper reports nowhere are missing: `by_cause` counts them and `listed` names the first 15 of each cause as `file: name`. The cause is what the item's file shows, so it says where to look, not what is wrong:

| Cause | The file shows |
| --- | --- |
| `compound_member` | An assignment to a member of another component (`Form.List = List`). |
| `object_member` | The name as a function-valued key of an object literal (`logo: () => ...`). |
| `dependency` | An alias of something a package exports (`const Tooltip = Recharts.Tooltip`), or an export that ends in a package. |
| `call_result` | A value a call builds (`createIcon(...)`, `generateCalendar(...)`). |
| `file_with_other_components`, `file_without_components` | A declaration Caliper does not report, in a file where it reports others, or none. |

The 14 antd items still unpaired in the weekly run of 2026-11-06 (16 when this was first written) are not pairing cases: the date picker and calendar families (built by factory functions), `Parent.Member` entries Caliper reports under the parent (`Form.List`, `Mentions.Option`, `TreeSelect.TreeNode`), and helpers RDT lists as components (`confirm`, `dropIndicator`). shadcn has no re-export of this kind in the pinned commit, so nothing pairs there; its unpaired items are `Icons.logo`-style object members, aliases such as `const ComboboxRoot = Primitive.Root` and factory results, which Caliper does not detect.

73:## The checker is the default (S8)
74-
75-S8 turns the checker on by default (`--no-checker` and `checker: false` turn it off). Measured 2026-11-12 on `feat/checker-is-default` against `main` at `8212aef8`, release builds, the built-in checker (tsrs crates `0.24.0`), macOS 27.3 on an Apple M5 Max, a shared machine at load 8 to 21. Scratch inputs are under `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default`.
76-
77-- **Whole-project `extract`** (`extract --src <dir> --json --quiet --no-cache`, otherwise the CLI's defaults; wall time and peak RSS from `time -l`, 3 interleaved runs each, ranges):
78-  - `gate-large`, 938 Chakra and MUI wrappers: **6.05 to 10.56 s, 966 to 974 MiB** by default (the 10.56 s run was the first, at the highest load; the other two 6.05 s). `--no-checker`: 0.09 to 0.10 s, 201 to 203 MiB. `main` gave 0.09 to 0.10 s and 196 to 198 MiB by default, and 6.18 to 8.33 s and 968 to 973 MiB with `--experimental-semantic-types`.
79-  - The 787 Chakra wrappers alone: **5.37 to 5.55 s, 765 to 776 MiB** by default; `--no-checker` 0.07 to 0.08 s, 158 MiB; `main`'s `--experimental-semantic-types` 5.37 to 5.50 s, 759 to 772 MiB.
80-  - Three renamed copies of `gate-large` (2,814 components, one run): 15.4 s and 1,053 MiB by default, 0.14 s and 228 MiB with `--no-checker`. Memory hardly grows with the component count: the whole-project pass holds one program and interns equal props across components, so no `extract` measured here comes near 2 GB.
81-  - Output: the default's canonical JSON equals `main`'s `--experimental-semantic-types` once `stats` is set aside, and `--no-checker`'s equals `main`'s default but for one help text (`OPAQUE_TYPE`'s hint now names `--no-checker`).
82-  - Not measured: the five corpora of `docs/measurement.md`, which are not installed here (no corpus was fetched for this).
83-- **A session's kept answers** (the Storybook addon's configuration through the native binding: lazy, dependencies loaded, nothing collapsed, `semanticWaitMs` and `semanticWaitEmptyMs` 60 s so every answer is the checker's; `gate-large`'s components asked one at a time, the process's RSS read every 100). Each checker answer is kept for the next request, and each held its own copy of every prop: 1,257, 1,930 and 2,602 MiB after 100, 200 and 300 components, about 6.7 MiB per Chakra component (trail 369 slice 2 read 5,365 MiB at 900). With the checker on by default a session that asked for every story would run out of memory, so the answer cache now shares one copy of each equal prop per generation (`AnswerCache::shared` in `crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`), as the whole-project merge does: 716, 786 and 825 MiB at 100, 200 and 300, **1,007 MiB after all 938, peak 1,058 MiB**. The structural session alone (`checker: false`) peaks at 377 MiB.
84-- **Budgets, per trail 333.** The first answer keeps its 150 ms budget for a story that was prefetched or answered before (the addon's `prefetchStories`, then the kept answer); the cold first answer is recorded rather than gated: `ChakraButton` median **171 ms** in process (169 to 173, trail 369 slice 2), against 277 ms over the pipe. Watch keeps 25 ms for the checker's own part (own props: p95 6.3 ms in process), and records the `ButtonProps` form: **p95 162.3 ms** (p50 157.7, p99 168.5), whose floor is converting its 1,138 props.
85-
86-## Startup prefetch (trail 332)
87-
88-- **The gate.** In a real Storybook 11 run on Chakra, the first story has the checker's props within 150 ms of the browser's request when the prefetch started at least as long before it as the component's cold cost; a story outside the prefetch is no slower than without it; peak memory at most 30 MB above.
89-- **How it reaches Storybook.** Storybook 11 starts its docgen worker on the first `extractDocgen` (`createDocgenWorkerClient`: `worker ??= new DocgenWorker`), so nothing in the worker runs earlier. The addon's preset adds an `experimental_devServer` hook, which Storybook applies before the builders start; after Storybook's own hook registers the `core/docgen` service, it reads the story index and calls `getService('core/docgen', { internal: true }).commands.extractDocgen({ id })` (`storybook/internal/core-server`, internal API, Storybook `11.0.0-alpha.9`) for the opening story's component. The command runs the provider chain and writes the answer to the service's state, which the manager receives with its first sync. The manager's Controls panel subscribes once the story is prepared; that subscription's load calls `extractDocgen` again, so the provider is asked a second time and answers from the session, but `isInitialLoading` is false while the stored payload is there, so the panel shows it at once.
90-- **Harness.** `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/prefetch`: `storybook dev` (11.0.0-alpha.9, Vite 8, `@storybook/builder-vite` 10.6.2 from the pnpm store with its mock extraction stubbed, since the store has no 11 builder) over 40 stories of `gate-large`'s Chakra wrappers with a `ChakraProvider` decorator, `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` on the pinned tsrs and `fallback: 'never'`. Playwright opens the root URL as soon as `index.json` answers, as `storybook dev` opens the browser once the index is built. The browser's request and answer times are the manager's websocket frames (`services:command-invoke` for `extractDocgen`, the `core/docgen` state entry); a provider registered after the addon's logs each request in the worker. Shared machine at load 20 to 160; 13 runs with the prefetch (9 of one story, 4 of three) and 9 without, interleaved.
91-- **Lead time.** The browser asked 1.5 to 6.3 s after the server was spawned (median 2.2 s), 0.8 to 2.3 s after the prefetch started (median 1.2 s); the prefetch starts 45 to 120 ms after the index is built. `ChakraButton` cold through the prefetch took 0.57 to 2.2 s (median 1.0 s): the opening story fits before the browser asks, a second large component does not.
92-- **Result.** In every run where the prefetch started at least its cold cost before the request (9 runs, and one whose prefetch start was not logged), the checker's 1,137 props were in the browser from 84 ms before to 92 ms after its request (median 10 ms before). Where it had not (3 runs at high load), they arrived 246 to 308 ms after it. Without the prefetch they arrived 0.74 to 2.9 s after the request (median 1.6 s), and once, at load 159, the story got 0 props after its 2 s wait. **PASS.**
93-- **A story outside the prefetch.** Opened 10 s later: 0.45 to 1.4 s with (median 0.82 s) against 0.64 to 2.1 s without (median 1.0 s). Opened directly at startup, competing with the prefetch: 0.5 to 2.2 s with (median 1.1 s) against 0.82 to 1.7 s without (median 1.35 s). **PASS** in the median; the slowest single value is with the prefetch, at the highest load.
94-- **Memory.** The Storybook process tree (Node and tsrs), opening the first story: peak 752 to 825 MiB with one story prefetched (median 767) against 720 to 764 without (median 750): **+17 MiB** by median, +22 in each of the two interleaved series; at idle 10 s later within noise. Prefetching 3 stories held about 200 MiB more at idle and made a story opened at startup slower (median 2.2 s), which is why the default is 1.
95-- **Found on the way.** Storybook hands a preset its own options merged with the addon's; its own `cache` (a file-system cache object) reached the native session as the addon's `cache`, which it refused, so the addon could not start in any real `storybook dev` until the preset dropped a non-boolean `cache`. And with the default `fallback: 'degraded'`, `ChakraButton` is handed to React's docgen even when the checker answers, because the structural warning that `Button` was not found stays on the answer.
96-
97-## Not covered
98-
99-- Other platforms: both measurements ran on macOS arm64. The Linux CI run is a separate gate.
100-- Wall time was not part of the question; a run takes about 0.5 s per edit here.
101-- The per-edit `ps` sampling reads the answering process after its reply, so a process that peaked inside a request and shrank before the sample is under-read.

73:## The checker is the default (S8)
74-
75-S8 turns the checker on by default (`--no-checker` and `checker: false` turn it off). Measured 2026-11-12 on `feat/checker-is-default` against `main` at `8212aef8`, release builds, the built-in checker (tsrs crates `0.24.0`), macOS 27.3 on an Apple M5 Max, a shared machine at load 8 to 21. Scratch inputs are under `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default`.
76-
77-- **Whole-project `extract`** (`extract --src <dir> --json --quiet --no-cache`, otherwise the CLI's defaults; wall time and peak RSS from `time -l`, 3 interleaved runs each, ranges):
78-  - `gate-large`, 938 Chakra and MUI wrappers: **6.05 to 10.56 s, 966 to 974 MiB** by default (the 10.56 s run was the first, at the highest load; the other two 6.05 s). `--no-checker`: 0.09 to 0.10 s, 201 to 203 MiB. `main` gave 0.09 to 0.10 s and 196 to 198 MiB by default, and 6.18 to 8.33 s and 968 to 973 MiB with `--experimental-semantic-types`.
79-  - The 787 Chakra wrappers alone: **5.37 to 5.55 s, 765 to 776 MiB** by default; `--no-checker` 0.07 to 0.08 s, 158 MiB; `main`'s `--experimental-semantic-types` 5.37 to 5.50 s, 759 to 772 MiB.
80-  - Three renamed copies of `gate-large` (2,814 components, one run): 15.4 s and 1,053 MiB by default, 0.14 s and 228 MiB with `--no-checker`. Memory hardly grows with the component count: the whole-project pass holds one program and interns equal props across components, so no `extract` measured here comes near 2 GB.
81-  - Output: the default's canonical JSON equals `main`'s `--experimental-semantic-types` once `stats` is set aside, and `--no-checker`'s equals `main`'s default but for one help text (`OPAQUE_TYPE`'s hint now names `--no-checker`).
82-  - Not measured: the five corpora of `docs/measurement.md`, which are not installed here (no corpus was fetched for this).
83-- **A session's kept answers** (the Storybook addon's configuration through the native binding: lazy, dependencies loaded, nothing collapsed, `semanticWaitMs` and `semanticWaitEmptyMs` 60 s so every answer is the checker's; `gate-large`'s components asked one at a time, the process's RSS read every 100). Each checker answer is kept for the next request, and each held its own copy of every prop: 1,257, 1,930 and 2,602 MiB after 100, 200 and 300 components, about 6.7 MiB per Chakra component (trail 369 slice 2 read 5,365 MiB at 900). With the checker on by default a session that asked for every story would run out of memory, so the answer cache now shares one copy of each equal prop per generation (`AnswerCache::shared` in `crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`), as the whole-project merge does: 716, 786 and 825 MiB at 100, 200 and 300, **1,007 MiB after all 938, peak 1,058 MiB**. The structural session alone (`checker: false`) peaks at 377 MiB.
84-- **Budgets, per trail 333.** The first answer keeps its 150 ms budget for a story that was prefetched or answered before (the addon's `prefetchStories`, then the kept answer); the cold first answer is recorded rather than gated: `ChakraButton` median **171 ms** in process (169 to 173, trail 369 slice 2), against 277 ms over the pipe. Watch keeps 25 ms for the checker's own part (own props: p95 6.3 ms in process), and records the `ButtonProps` form: **p95 162.3 ms** (p50 157.7, p99 168.5), whose floor is converting its 1,138 props.
85-
86-## Startup prefetch (trail 332)
87-
88-- **The gate.** In a real Storybook 11 run on Chakra, the first story has the checker's props within 150 ms of the browser's request when the prefetch started at least as long before it as the component's cold cost; a story outside the prefetch is no slower than without it; peak memory at most 30 MB above.
89-- **How it reaches Storybook.** Storybook 11 starts its docgen worker on the first `extractDocgen` (`createDocgenWorkerClient`: `worker ??= new DocgenWorker`), so nothing in the worker runs earlier. The addon's preset adds an `experimental_devServer` hook, which Storybook applies before the builders start; after Storybook's own hook registers the `core/docgen` service, it reads the story index and calls `getService('core/docgen', { internal: true }).commands.extractDocgen({ id })` (`storybook/internal/core-server`, internal API, Storybook `11.0.0-alpha.9`) for the opening story's component. The command runs the provider chain and writes the answer to the service's state, which the manager receives with its first sync. The manager's Controls panel subscribes once the story is prepared; that subscription's load calls `extractDocgen` again, so the provider is asked a second time and answers from the session, but `isInitialLoading` is false while the stored payload is there, so the panel shows it at once.
90-- **Harness.** `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/prefetch`: `storybook dev` (11.0.0-alpha.9, Vite 8, `@storybook/builder-vite` 10.6.2 from the pnpm store with its mock extraction stubbed, since the store has no 11 builder) over 40 stories of `gate-large`'s Chakra wrappers with a `ChakraProvider` decorator, `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` on the pinned tsrs and `fallback: 'never'`. Playwright opens the root URL as soon as `index.json` answers, as `storybook dev` opens the browser once the index is built. The browser's request and answer times are the manager's websocket frames (`services:command-invoke` for `extractDocgen`, the `core/docgen` state entry); a provider registered after the addon's logs each request in the worker. Shared machine at load 20 to 160; 13 runs with the prefetch (9 of one story, 4 of three) and 9 without, interleaved.
91-- **Lead time.** The browser asked 1.5 to 6.3 s after the server was spawned (median 2.2 s), 0.8 to 2.3 s after the prefetch started (median 1.2 s); the prefetch starts 45 to 120 ms after the index is built. `ChakraButton` cold through the prefetch took 0.57 to 2.2 s (median 1.0 s): the opening story fits before the browser asks, a second large component does not.
92-- **Result.** In every run where the prefetch started at least its cold cost before the request (9 runs, and one whose prefetch start was not logged), the checker's 1,137 props were in the browser from 84 ms before to 92 ms after its request (median 10 ms before). Where it had not (3 runs at high load), they arrived 246 to 308 ms after it. Without the prefetch they arrived 0.74 to 2.9 s after the request (median 1.6 s), and once, at load 159, the story got 0 props after its 2 s wait. **PASS.**
93-- **A story outside the prefetch.** Opened 10 s later: 0.45 to 1.4 s with (median 0.82 s) against 0.64 to 2.1 s without (median 1.0 s). Opened directly at startup, competing with the prefetch: 0.5 to 2.2 s with (median 1.1 s) against 0.82 to 1.7 s without (median 1.35 s). **PASS** in the median; the slowest single value is with the prefetch, at the highest load.
94-- **Memory.** The Storybook process tree (Node and tsrs), opening the first story: peak 752 to 825 MiB with one story prefetched (median 767) against 720 to 764 without (median 750): **+17 MiB** by median, +22 in each of the two interleaved series; at idle 10 s later within noise. Prefetching 3 stories held about 200 MiB more at idle and made a story opened at startup slower (median 2.2 s), which is why the default is 1.
95-- **Found on the way.** Storybook hands a preset its own options merged with the addon's; its own `cache` (a file-system cache object) reached the native session as the addon's `cache`, which it refused, so the addon could not start in any real `storybook dev` until the preset dropped a non-boolean `cache`. And with the default `fallback: 'degraded'`, `ChakraButton` is handed to React's docgen even when the checker answers, because the structural warning that `Button` was not found stays on the answer.
96-
97-## Not covered
98-
99-- Other platforms: both measurements ran on macOS arm64. The Linux CI run is a separate gate.
100-- Wall time was not part of the question; a run takes about 0.5 s per edit here.
101-- The per-edit `ps` sampling reads the answering process after its reply, so a process that peaked inside a request and shrank before the sample is under-read.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The weekly headline: how correct the types are that Storybook and agents are shown, and when to open an issue.

The headline is read from what the oracle already measured (apps/oracle/src/tool-universe.ts `caliper_reported`): every
own prop TypeScript 7.1's checker finds on a component Caliper reports, each judged against the checker. A prop is
correct (the same type, or the same type spelled differently), less precise (vaguer than the checker's, not
contradicting it), wrong (describing something else), without a checker type (the checker has none either), not judged
(the oracle did not evaluate the checker's type, so nothing was compared), missing (Caliper reports the component but
not the prop), or named only (Caliper lists it by name as a member of a collapsed inheritance layer, so it is surfaced
but has no type to judge).

This module holds the arithmetic and the issue conditions so scripts/weekly.py only calls it. Matching react-docgen-
typescript (recall) is information, never a gate.
"""
import oracle_data

# The gate. Of the props Caliper lists whose type can be judged against the checker's, more than this share wrong opens
# an issue, and so does any rise from the last record: a wrong type in Storybook is the one thing a reader cannot see.
WRONG_GATE = 0.001

# User-facing budgets for one whole run (process start included) over a pinned corpus with dependencies loaded, the
# default. They are not week-over-week limits: a shared CI machine drifts by 10% or more on its own, and a drift that
# stays inside the budget is not a problem. Chakra, the largest corpus, runs in about 1 s and 446 MiB.
BUDGETS = {'ms': 2000, 'rss_mib': 600}
BUDGET_LABELS = {'ms': 'time', 'rss_mib': 'peak memory'}
BUDGET_UNITS = {'ms': 'ms', 'rss_mib': 'MiB'}

# The keys of one corpus's headline, in the order the summary prints them.
KINDS = ('correct', 'less_precise', 'wrong', 'no_checker_type', 'not_judged', 'missing', 'named_only')

# The headline key each verdict of the oracle (apps/oracle/src/vocabulary.ts) is counted under; the verdicts that say
# Caliper's type is the checker's are `correct`. A verdict that is in neither is a KeyError, not a prop that vanishes.
VERDICT_KINDS = {'less precise': 'less_precise', 'wrong': 'wrong', 'checker any/error': 'no_checker_type',
                 'not judged': 'not_judged'}


def kind_of(verdict):
    return 'correct' if verdict in oracle_data.AGREE else VERDICT_KINDS[verdict]


def compute(oracle):
    """The headline of one corpus from its oracle entry, or None when the oracle did not run, failed, or is a record from
    before the headline existed (it has no `caliper_reported`)."""
    scored = ((oracle or {}).get('tools') or {}).get('caliper_reported')
    if not scored:
        return None
    verdicts, reasons = scored['verdicts'], scored['missing_by_reason']
    counts = {kind: 0 for kind in KINDS}
    for verdict in oracle_data.VERDICTS:
        counts[kind_of(verdict)] += verdicts[verdict]
    counts['missing'] = reasons['prop']
    counts['named_only'] = reasons['collapsed']
    # A component Caliper reports is never missing for want of the component, and Caliper never throws on a file; both
    # are zero here, and counted if they are not so the parts always add up to the whole.
    other = scored['universe'] - sum(counts.values())
    return {'components': scored['components'], 'props': scored['universe'], **counts, **({'other': other} if other else {})}


def judged(h):
    """The props Caliper lists whose type can be judged: correct, less precise or wrong."""
def own_metric(entry, key):
    """Caliper's own `key` ('ms' or 'rss_mib') of a corpus entry, or None when it is absent or not Caliper's own."""
    return own_peak(entry) if key == 'rss_mib' else (entry.get('caliper') or {}).get(key)


def findings(name, entry, previous):
    """What opens the issue for one corpus: a wrong type above the gate or higher than last week, or a whole run over a
    budget. `previous` is the corpus entry of the last record, or None."""
    out = []
    h = entry.get('headline')
    if h:
        rate = wrong_rate(h)
        old = (previous or {}).get('headline')
        rose = old is not None and rate > wrong_rate(old) + 1e-9
        was = f", up from {old['wrong']:,} of {judged(old):,}, {100 * wrong_rate(old):.2f}% last week" if rose else ''
        if rate > WRONG_GATE:
            out.append(f"{name}: {h['wrong']:,} of the {judged(h):,} props whose type can be judged are wrong, "
                       f"{100 * rate:.2f}%{was}; the gate is {100 * WRONG_GATE:.1f}%")
        elif rose:
            out.append(f"{name}: wrong types rose to {h['wrong']:,} of {judged(h):,}, {100 * rate:.2f}%{was}")
    for key, budget in BUDGETS.items():
        value = own_metric(entry, key)
        if value is not None and value > budget:
            out.append(f"{name}: a whole run's {BUDGET_LABELS[key]} is {value:,} {BUDGET_UNITS[key]}, over the "
                       f"{budget:,} {BUDGET_UNITS[key]} budget")
    return out


HOW_TO_READ = (
    'How to read these numbers. The headline asks one question: for the components Caliper reports, are the types in its '
    "output right? Each prop is judged against TypeScript 7.1's checker, which is the truth here, not against another "
    'tool. A prop that Caliper lists only by name in a collapsed inheritance layer is surfaced, but a reader sees no type '
    'for it, so it is counted apart. Recall against react-docgen-typescript (RDT) asks a different question, how much '
    'of what RDT reports Caliper also reports; it is information, because RDT is itself wrong on some props. Gates, '
    f'which open an issue: more than {100 * WRONG_GATE:.1f}% wrong (or any rise), a silent-wrong answer to a question a '
    f"reader is asked, or a whole run over {BUDGETS['ms'] / 1000:.0f} s or {BUDGETS['rss_mib']} MiB. Time and memory "
    'drift from week to week is shown, not alarmed on.'
)

DEFINITIONS = (
    'Correct: the same type as the checker, or the same type spelled differently. Less precise: vaguer than the '
    "checker's (a name left unexpanded, `string` for a union of literals), not contradicting it. Wrong: describes "
    'something else; this is the gate. No checker type: the checker has none either (an unresolved import, `any`). '
    "Not judged: the oracle did not evaluate the checker's type (it was cut at the depth limit, or is a kind the "
    'oracle does not read), so nothing was compared; it is neither agreement nor a difference. '
    'Missing: Caliper reports the component but not the prop. Named only: listed by name in a collapsed layer, with no '
    'type to judge.'
)


def markdown(record):


def tool_run(command, out):
    """One whole run of a Node tool that writes its components to `out`: wall ms, peak RSS MiB and the components."""
    seconds, rss = run_once(command)
    with open(out) as f:
        return {'ms': round(seconds * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(rss)}, json.load(f)['components']


def caliper_run(binary, src, runs):
    """Median wall ms and largest peak RSS MiB of `extract --json` in the Storybook addon's configuration (dependencies
    loaded, inherited props not collapsed), and the JSON's size. Every run here is the structural resolver's
    (`--no-checker`): the record and its budgets predate the checker default (docs/measurement.md)."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none',
               '--no-checker']
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as out:
        run_once(command, stdout=out)
        size = out.tell()
    samples = [run_once(command) for _ in range(runs)]
    return {'ms': round(statistics.median(s for s, _ in samples) * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(max(r for _, r in samples)),
            'json_mb': round(size / 2**20, 2)}


def caliper_components(binary, src, root):
    """Caliper's components in RDT's format, as (file, name) -> prop names."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--format', 'rdt', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported',
               '--quiet', '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none', '--no-checker']
    out = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    return {(relative(c['filePath'], root), norm_name(c['displayName'])): set(c['props'])
            for c in json.loads(out[out.index('{'):]).values()}


def caliper_layer_members(binary, src, root):
    """The props Caliper's collapsed inheritance layers hold, as (file, name) -> prop names: the output names them in a
    layer instead of listing them as props, and the canonical JSON is the one that carries the layers."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported', '--quiet',
               '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none', '--no-checker']
    out = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    document = schema_version.check(json.loads(out[out.index('{'):]), 'weekly')
    lists = document.get('nameLists', {})
    members = {}
    for c in document['components'].values():
        names = set()
        for layer in c.get('inheritance', []):
            if layer.get('members'):
                names |= set(lists[layer['members']])


def oracle_tools(tools):
    """The oracle's score for each tool, without the examples that are there to review the adapters by."""
    return {tool: {key: value for key, value in score.items() if key != 'examples'} for tool, score in tools.items()}


def oracle(binary, name, src, root, work, rdt_out, rdg_out):
    """How often TypeScript 7.1's checker contradicts Caliper's prop types (apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts), and how RDT and
    react-docgen fare against it over the same props. `shared_props`, `agree` and `wrong` are Caliper's, over the props
    both list, and keep their meaning from week to week (a prop the checker side did not evaluate is in `shared_props`
    and counts toward neither `agree` nor `wrong`, as `verdicts['not judged']`); `tools` holds all three over every prop of the candidate
    components the checker finds (the functions `exclusion`'s shape rules take out are left out: `universe_excluded`), and
    `tools_all_functions` the same scores over every function the checker takes for a component, as `tools` was before
    `universe_version` 2."""
    caliper_json = os.path.join(work, f'{name}.caliper.json')
    with open(caliper_json, 'w') as f:
        subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported',
                        '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none', '--quiet', '--no-checker'],
                       stdout=f, check=True)
    list_file, tsconfig = program_inputs(name, src, work)
    verdicts = os.path.join(work, f'{name}.oracle.json')
    subprocess.run(['pnpm', '--dir', os.path.join(ROOT, 'apps', 'oracle'), 'exec', 'tsx', 'src/oracle.ts', '--root', root,
                    '--src', src, '--tsconfig', tsconfig, '--caliper', caliper_json, '--out', verdicts, '--files',
                    list_file, '--rdt', rdt_out, '--rdg', rdg_out], check=True, timeout=3600)
    with open(verdicts) as f:
        e = json.load(f)
    shared = e['props_shared']
    return {'shared_props': shared, 'agree': rate((sum(e['verdicts'][v] for v in oracle_data.AGREE), shared)),
            'wrong': rate((e['verdicts']['wrong'], shared)), 'universe_version': UNIVERSE_VERSION,
            'tools': oracle_tools(e['tools']), 'tools_all_functions': oracle_tools(e['tools_all_functions']),
            'universe_excluded': e['universe_excluded']}


def measure(args, corpus, work):
    root = os.path.join(os.path.abspath(args.corpora), corpus['clone'])

own prop TypeScript 7.1's checker finds on a component Caliper reports, each judged against the checker. A prop is
correct (the same type, or the same type spelled differently), less precise (vaguer than the checker's, not
contradicting it), wrong (describing something else), without a checker type (the checker has none either), not judged
(the oracle did not evaluate the checker's type, so nothing was compared), missing (Caliper reports the component but
not the prop), or named only (Caliper lists it by name as a member of a collapsed inheritance layer, so it is surfaced
but has no type to judge).

This module holds the arithmetic and the issue conditions so scripts/weekly.py only calls it. Matching react-docgen-
typescript (recall) is information, never a gate.
"""
import oracle_data

# The gate. Of the props Caliper lists whose type can be judged against the checker's, more than this share wrong opens
# an issue, and so does any rise from the last record: a wrong type in Storybook is the one thing a reader cannot see.
WRONG_GATE = 0.001

# User-facing budgets for one whole run (process start included) over a pinned corpus with dependencies loaded, the
# default. They are not week-over-week limits: a shared CI machine drifts by 10% or more on its own, and a drift that
# stays inside the budget is not a problem. Chakra, the largest corpus, runs in about 1 s and 446 MiB.
BUDGETS = {'ms': 2000, 'rss_mib': 600}
BUDGET_LABELS = {'ms': 'time', 'rss_mib': 'peak memory'}
BUDGET_UNITS = {'ms': 'ms', 'rss_mib': 'MiB'}

# The keys of one corpus's headline, in the order the summary prints them.
KINDS = ('correct', 'less_precise', 'wrong', 'no_checker_type', 'not_judged', 'missing', 'named_only')

# The headline key each verdict of the oracle (apps/oracle/src/vocabulary.ts) is counted under; the verdicts that say
# Caliper's type is the checker's are `correct`. A verdict that is in neither is a KeyError, not a prop that vanishes.
VERDICT_KINDS = {'less precise': 'less_precise', 'wrong': 'wrong', 'checker any/error': 'no_checker_type',
                 'not judged': 'not_judged'}


def kind_of(verdict):
    return 'correct' if verdict in oracle_data.AGREE else VERDICT_KINDS[verdict]


def compute(oracle):
    """The headline of one corpus from its oracle entry, or None when the oracle did not run, failed, or is a record from
    before the headline existed (it has no `caliper_reported`)."""
    scored = ((oracle or {}).get('tools') or {}).get('caliper_reported')
    if not scored:
        return None
    verdicts, reasons = scored['verdicts'], scored['missing_by_reason']
    counts = {kind: 0 for kind in KINDS}
    for verdict in oracle_data.VERDICTS:
        counts[kind_of(verdict)] += verdicts[verdict]
    counts['missing'] = reasons['prop']
    counts['named_only'] = reasons['collapsed']
    # A component Caliper reports is never missing for want of the component, and Caliper never throws on a file; both
    # are zero here, and counted if they are not so the parts always add up to the whole.
    other = scored['universe'] - sum(counts.values())
    return {'components': scored['components'], 'props': scored['universe'], **counts, **({'other': other} if other else {})}

name: Weekly

# Caliper, react-docgen-typescript and react-docgen on five public repos with their dependencies installed: time,
# memory and recall (docs/measurement.md), and how often a reader of Caliper's output answers a fixed list of questions
# wrong without a hint (scripts/agent_eval.py). Its headline is how many of the props of the components Caliper reports
# are right against the checker (scripts/headline.py). It opens or updates one issue when a wrong type is above the gate or
# rises, when a silent-wrong answer appears, or when a whole run is over a budget; drift in time, memory and recall against
# RDT is listed in the summary and does not open one. It never runs on a pull request and never fails one.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"

jobs:
  weekly:
    name: Weekly
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      # The corpora's own package managers run under Node 24: Yarn 4.18, which Mantine and React Spectrum pin, crashes
      # under the repository's Node 26 ("Dynamic require of "util" is not supported"). This step comes before the
      # toolchain's so that the toolchain's Node stays first on PATH for everything else; only the installs use this one.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          package-manager-cache: false
      - id: corpus-node
        run: echo "dir=$(dirname "$(command -v node)")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # RDT, react-docgen and the oracle run from apps/oracle's dependencies.
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:
          auto-install: true
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-pnpm-cache@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
      # About 10 GB of installed node_modules is too large to cache; the package managers' stores are not.
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .corpora/caches
          key: weekly-${{ hashFiles('scripts/corpora.py', 'pnpm-lock.yaml') }}
      # A corpus that fails to install is named in the log with the tail of the install log; the others still install.
      - name: Fetch and install the corpora
        env:
          INSTALL_NODE_DIR: ${{ steps.corpus-node.outputs.dir }}
        run: python3 scripts/corpora.py setup --install-node-dir "$INSTALL_NODE_DIR"
      - name: Fetch last week's record
        id: baseline
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        # A first run has no earlier run to download; a download that fails is a different thing and has to show: it
        # leaves an error annotation and a line in the summary, and fails this step. The job still measures, tells
        # weekly.py (`--baseline-failed`, which opens the issue) and then fails in the last step.
        run: |
          id=$(gh run list --workflow weekly.yml --status success --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId // empty')
          if [ -z "$id" ]; then
            echo "::notice::No earlier successful run exists, so there is no baseline to compare with."

      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:

      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

# usage: measure.sh <label> <runs> <binary> <src> [extra args...]
label=$1; runs=$2; bin=$3; src=$4; shift 4

  /usr/bin/time -l "$bin" extract --src "$src" --json --quiet --no-cache "$@" > /dev/null 2> "$TMPDIR/m.err"

  wall=$(awk '/ real / {print $1}' "$TMPDIR/m.err")
  echo "$label run=$i exit=$code wall_s=$wall peak_mib=$rss"

class OnlyCaliperOwnNumbersOpenAnIssueForCost(unittest.TestCase):
    """The issue opens when a whole run of Caliper is over its budget (scripts/headline.py BUDGETS), never because a number
    moved from last week and never because of another tool's numbers."""

    def test_the_shape_of_issue_279_opens_nothing(self):
        now, before = shape_of_nov_2(), shape_of_nov_2()
        before['corpora']['shadcn']['caliper'].update(ms=607 // 2, rss_mib=1593)
        self.assertEqual(weekly.findings(now, before), [])

    def test_the_time_noise_of_issue_279_is_a_change_and_not_a_finding(self):
        before = {'corpora': {'shadcn': {'caliper': {'ms': 458, 'rss_mib': 334}}}}
        now = {'corpora': {'shadcn': {'caliper': {'ms': 607, 'rss_mib': 334}}}}
        self.assertEqual(weekly.findings(now, before), [])
        self.assertEqual(weekly.changes(now, before), ['shadcn: time 458 -> 607'])

    def test_a_rise_in_only_the_comparison_tools_is_not_in_the_issue_or_the_changes(self):
        before, now = shape_of_nov_2(), shape_of_nov_2()
        for r in (before, now):
            r['corpora']['antd']['caliper']['rss_mib'] = 152
        for tool in ('rdt', 'react_docgen'):
            now['corpora']['antd'][tool].update(ms=60000, rss_mib=5000)
        self.assertEqual(weekly.findings(now, before), [])
        self.assertEqual(weekly.changes(now, before), [])

    def test_a_caliper_run_over_a_budget_opens_one_issue_line_per_metric(self):
        now = shape_of_nov_2()
        now['corpora']['shadcn']['caliper'].update(ms=2500, rss_mib=700)
        now['corpora']['shadcn']['rdt']['rss_mib'] = 1394
        out = weekly.findings(now, {'corpora': {}})
        self.assertEqual(len(out), 2)
        self.assertTrue(all(line.startswith('shadcn: a whole run') for line in out))

    def test_one_peak_for_every_tool_is_not_read_as_caliper_s(self):
        """The 11-02 shape: 1901 MiB for all three tools is the helper's process-wide maximum, so no budget or change is read
        from it, though a time moving 11 to 33% on its own is still a change."""
        before = shape_of_nov_2()
        before['corpora']['shadcn']['caliper'].update(ms=300, rss_mib=1593)
        before['corpora']['shadcn']['rdt']['rss_mib'] = 1593
        before['corpora']['shadcn']['react_docgen']['rss_mib'] = 1593
        self.assertEqual(weekly.findings(shape_of_nov_2(), before), [])
        self.assertEqual(weekly.changes(shape_of_nov_2(), before), ['shadcn: time 300 -> 458'])

    def test_the_largest_corpus_stays_inside_the_budget_with_its_own_spread(self):
        """Chakra's peak was 446, 451 and 555 MiB in three records; the budget has to hold all three."""
        for rss in (446, 451, 555):
            now = {'corpora': {'chakra': {'caliper': {'ms': 1048, 'rss_mib': rss}}}}
            self.assertEqual(weekly.findings(now, now), [])

    def test_a_missing_metric_does_not_crash_the_rule(self):
        before = {'corpora': {'antd': {'caliper': {'ms': 100}}}}
        now = {'corpora': {'antd': {'caliper': {'rss_mib': 100}}, 'mantine': {}}}
        self.assertEqual(weekly.findings(now, before), [])
        self.assertEqual(weekly.changes(now, before), [])
        self.assertEqual(weekly.changes({'corpora': {'antd': {}}}, {'corpora': {'antd': {'caliper': {'ms': 1}}}}), [])


class MeasureHelperErrors(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_command_that_cannot_run_names_itself(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, r'no-such-command-here exited with 127: cannot run no-such-command-here'):
            corpora.run_once(['no-such-command-here'])

    def test_exit_code_and_stderr_are_reported(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, r'exited with 3: oops'):
                         ['antd: wrong types rose to 1 of 1,000, 0.10%, up from 0 of 999, 0.00% last week'])

    def test_inside_the_gate_and_not_rising_is_quiet(self):
        h = {**HEADLINE, 'correct': 899, 'less_precise': 100, 'wrong': 1}
        self.assertEqual(headline.findings('antd', entry(h), None), [])
        self.assertEqual(headline.findings('antd', entry(h), entry(h)), [])
        self.assertEqual(headline.findings('antd', entry(h), entry({**h, 'wrong': 2})), [])

    def test_a_whole_run_over_a_budget_opens_an_issue(self):
        self.assertEqual(headline.findings('chakra', entry(ms=2500, rss_mib=700), None),
                         ['chakra: a whole run\'s time is 2,500 ms, over the 2,000 ms budget',
                          "chakra: a whole run's peak memory is 700 MiB, over the 600 MiB budget"])

    def test_a_run_inside_the_budget_is_quiet_however_much_it_drifted(self):
        self.assertEqual(headline.findings('chakra', entry(ms=2000, rss_mib=600), entry(ms=500, rss_mib=100)), [])

    def test_a_record_without_a_headline_or_without_numbers_is_quiet(self):
        self.assertEqual(headline.findings('antd', {}, None), [])
        self.assertEqual(headline.findings('antd', {'caliper': {}}, entry(HEADLINE)), [])


class Summary(unittest.TestCase):
    def record(self, **corpora):
        return {'caliper': 'x', 'runs': 1, 'reference_version': weekly.REFERENCE_VERSION, 'corpora': corpora}

    def test_it_explains_the_numbers_even_when_the_oracle_did_not_run(self):
        self.assertEqual(headline.markdown(self.record(antd=entry())), [headline.HOW_TO_READ, ''])

    def test_the_table_gives_each_kind_as_a_share_of_the_props(self):
        lines = headline.markdown(self.record(antd=entry(HEADLINE)))
        self.assertEqual(lines[2:4], ['### Headline: are the types Storybook shows right?', ''])
        self.assertEqual(lines[-4:-1], ['| Corpus | Props | Correct | Less precise | Wrong | No checker type | Not judged | Missing '
                                       '| Named only |',
                                       '| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |',
                                       '| antd | 1,000 | 80.0% | 10.0% | 0.20% | 0.8% | 0.0% | 3.0% | 6.0% |'])

    def test_an_oracle_that_failed_is_named(self):
        lines = headline.markdown(self.record(antd=entry(oracle={'error': 'tsx failed'})))
        self.assertIn('| antd | unavailable: tsx failed | | | | | | | |', lines)

    def test_the_budgets_and_the_gate_in_the_text_are_the_ones_used(self):
        self.assertIn('more than 0.1% wrong', headline.HOW_TO_READ)
        self.assertIn('over 2 s or 600 MiB', headline.HOW_TO_READ)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A/B speed and memory of this checkout (or a branch) against origin/main, for when a change touches the resolver.

cache on after a warm-up run, inherited props not collapsed) over Mantine and Chakra with their dependencies installed
(`scripts/corpora.py setup --corpus mantine --corpus chakra`; without them nothing would be loaded, so the run stops)
with the two builds interleaved and alternating which goes first, and prints the median wall time and peak RSS of each
side. The 1.10x time and 1.20x memory thresholds come from a calibration made with dependency loading and the cache
off (within 1.04 for time and 1.12 for memory with nothing changed); it has not been repeated in this configuration, so
treat them as a starting point. Nothing enforces them.

docs/performance.md:3:How fast Caliper is and what it costs is recorded in `docs/measurement.md`: a weekly run on five pinned corpora, and `just bench` for a change that touches the resolver. Both measure the structural resolver (`--no-checker`), which is the fallback since the checker became the default (ADR 0026 S8); the checker's cost is in `docs/gate-measurements.md` ("The checker is the default"). The criterion benches (`cargo bench -p caliper-docgen-core`) and `docs/benchmarks.md` cover single fixtures. This page keeps the measurements that explain where the time goes.
docs/performance.md:5:The per-pull-request scorecard that used to enforce these numbers is gone. It caught one real regression (Mantine 38% and Chakra 47% slower after a batch of 20 resolver pull requests merged on 2026-10-26, found by the weekly run), and its gates failed on runner noise and on bases that had moved. The figures below came from it and are history, not limits.
docs/performance.md:25:RDT's component and prop counts are not comparable with Caliper's here: without dependencies it reports every exported function and expands what it can of `@types/react`. Precision is in `docs/precision.md`; recall and agreement with RDT on installed repos are recorded weekly (`docs/measurement.md`).
docs/performance.md:44:RDT (`withCustomConfig`, `shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum`, `shouldRemoveUndefinedFromOptional`) took 1.6 to 27 s and 0.6 to 2.7 GB per repo. The harness that ran this is not in the repository; `scripts/weekly.py` records the same comparison.
docs/STATUS.md:14:- **Recall** against `react-docgen-typescript` with dependencies installed and loaded: the share of RDT's reference components and props that Caliper also reports, not a measure of correctness (the checker judges that; on the props both list, the checker contradicts Caliper on 0 to 1.09% and RDT on 0.006 to 5.02%, `docs/rdt-differences.md`, 2026-11-06). The weekly record and the current definition of the reference are in `docs/measurement.md`.
docs/STATUS.md:17:- **Speed, structural resolver (`--no-checker`)** on five pinned public corpora (`docs/performance.md`, 2026-10-22): 34 to 81 ms wall time and 66 to 153 MB peak RSS for 41 to 490 kLOC, 17 to 39 times faster than `react-docgen-typescript` on the same files; the 938 wrappers above take 0.10 s and 200 MiB. No pull-request gate enforces it: a weekly workflow records speed, memory and recall against RDT and react-docgen and opens an issue on a worsening, and `just bench` compares a branch with `main` locally (`docs/measurement.md`).
docs/STATUS.md:34:**The TypeScript checker is the default** (ADR 0026, S8 done 2026-11-12). `extract`, `check` and `inspect` merge the built-in checker's answer (the `tsrs` crates; `--tsc-path` runs a binary instead) over the structural one prop by prop, napi sessions and the Storybook addon ask it per component within `semanticWaitMs` (ADR 0022), and `--no-checker` (`checker: false`) turns it off; `watch` and the Vite plugin stay structural. A prop the checker could not read keeps the structural type with `degradedBy`, and a failed, crashed or timed-out checker falls back to the structural result with one warning. The gates before the flip (checker lane, determinism, Linux CI, memory past 600 edits, tsrs-against-Go parity) are recorded in ADR 0026. It began as the opt-in slice 1 (ADR 0006, ADR 0007, `type-checker-integration.md`), whose accuracy was verified against real RDT: 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches). TypeScript 7.1's Go checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/measurement.md`); the weekly record measures the structural resolver (`--no-checker`).
docs/STATUS.md:38:**Confidence routing (2026-10-25).** The idea: score each component's risk of wrong or missing props from Caliper's own output, and ask the TypeScript 7.1 checker only about the risky ones. Measured against the checker on 518,268 shared props over the five corpora and the fixtures, routing 10% of components caught 23% of the props only the checker reports with the existing warning rule (a component with a degrade warning or error), against 3% for a smoothed table and 6% for a logistic model. At a 20% budget neither model caught the one prop the oracle marks `wrong`. Most of the checker-only props were Next's ambient augmentation or false component matches, which a score of structural risk can't learn (the 1,154 of 1,182 on shadcn quoted then came from a run that no longer reproduces: the weekly record of 2026-11-06 finds 55 checker-only props on shadcn, all `tw`, and `docs/rdt-differences.md` has the current account). So no score ships: warnings stay the signal, and on-demand checker use asks about the requested component instead of predicting. The script was deleted, so the routing numbers above cannot be reproduced; the method is the oracle in `docs/measurement.md`.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:3:**Status:** the checker is the default ([ADR 0026](adr/0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md) S8, see "The checker is the default" below): `extract`, `check`, `inspect`, napi sessions and the Storybook addon ask it, and `--no-checker` (`checker: false`) turns it off. It began as an opt-in second resolver ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md), [ADR 0007](adr/0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md), "Slice 1" below); its answer wins prop by prop (see "The checker's answer wins"). The checker is built in (the `tsrs` crates, see "The checker"); `--tsc-path` runs a binary instead. Structural extraction is the fallback, and what `--no-checker`, `watch` and the Vite plugin run. Separately, TypeScript 7.1's checker runs as a test-only oracle for structural prop types (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`, `docs/measurement.md`). **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 for slice 1 against `7.1.0-beta`; 2026-09-27 for the Cost measurements, each naming its nightly; 2026-10-22 for the API table against the `7.1.0-beta` package; 2026-10-23 for the fixture-corpus parity on `7.1.0-beta`.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:89:Against the oracle (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`, flag on, `7.1.0-beta`), wrong verdicts fall to 0.0% on every corpus but antd (0.1%), but the identical-or-spelled share also falls: mantine 91.3% to 22.0%, chakra 100% to 16.4%, shadcn 85.2% to 52.3%, antd 91.9% to 82.3%, spectrum 83.2% to 28.3%. The oracle credits the structural result for keeping a type's name (`StyleProp<MantineSpacing>`); the checker's answer is expanded to its members and compared as "less precise". Keeping the alias name and arguments needs a `PropType` that carries them, which is an output change.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:227:- **Measured.** Spectrum (`extract --tsc-path <tsrs>` with the weekly's options, then behind `--experimental-semantic-types`): 3,877 of 4,112 unique props carry `parent` (3,764 of 4,102 before, taken from the structural pass). Of 11,384 props both runs list, 195 gained a `parent`, 29 lost one (the mapped case above) and 6 name the other of two interfaces that declare the prop (the checker's first declaration). `composes` is on 443 of 1,414 components (1,023 before, mostly `@react-types/shared` types the structural pass could not follow). On `gate-large`, 467,019 of the 467,221 props only the checker returns carry `parent`; the other 202 are members of type literals (Chakra's inline `{ axis?: … }`, `recipe`).
docs/type-checker-integration.md:238:- **Measured** (`extract` with the checker, then behind `--experimental-semantic-types`, with the weekly's options, tsrs `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, against the run before this slice). Before, the structural answer gave the order of 2,736 of Spectrum's 3,194 merged union props and 187 of gate-large's 432,813, and every default: on Spectrum 870 from code, 378 `@default` tags the checker also gives, 15 from the resolver only; on gate-large 499 tags. Now, Spectrum: 27 props gain a code default and none loses one; 11 of 3,686 unions change order, each to the written one (`focusMode?: 'child' | 'cell'`, `slot?: string | null`). With `--no-resolver-facts` 15 defaults (the mapped `@default` case above) and 22 more union orders (imported aliases) differ. gate-large: 834 props gain a default (the checker's `@default` tags of props only the checker returns) and none loses one; 1,452 of 432,690 unions take the written order (`translate?: 'yes' | 'no'`, `css`); with `--no-resolver-facts` no default and 16 more union orders differ (members through an import, such as MUI's `timeout?: TransitionProps['timeout'] | 'auto'`).
docs/type-checker-integration.md:249:- **Measurement and gates that stay structural.** The construct suite's structural lane, `scripts/weekly.py` (its time, memory, recall and oracle runs), `scripts/agent_eval.py` and `just bench` pass `--no-checker`: their expectations and budgets are the resolver's. The checker lane, which held the checker path before, now runs the default with `--tsc-path`.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:350:The removed harness's `compare.ts`/`analyze.ts` (caliper-docgen vs RDT/react-docgen) compared only name, `required`, type and default, and rendered our types themselves in `run-ours.ts` (objects print as `{ ... }`), so their type mismatches mixed resolver and renderer differences. Those limits went with it: `scripts/weekly.py` compares Caliper's own and `@types/react` props with RDT's by name, and the oracle compares prop types structurally against the TS 7.1 checker (`docs/measurement.md`).
AGENTS.md:55:No new sh, py or mjs script unless a CI job, the weekly or a documented recipe calls it; prefer a Rust test or the existing oracle TypeScript. A measurement run once is recorded in docs (`docs/measurement.md`, `docs/gate-measurements.md`), not committed as a script. Each script's caller is listed in `docs/measurement.md`.
docs/rdt-differences.md:7:Each class below has four parts: what differs, why we think Caliper is better (or "not better: a gap" and the fix direction), how the weekly record measures it (and whether the comparator scored it right), and how it is accounted for. The verdicts are `apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts` run on the same file (the oracle's own checker is `7.1.0-beta`). Caliper's output is the canonical JSON type with empty `description` fields dropped.
docs/rdt-differences.md:11:`scripts/weekly.py --oracle` extracts each pinned corpus with the flags above, then `apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts` asks TypeScript 7.1's checker for the type of every own prop of every exported function whose only parameter, or `props` parameter, is the props type. RDT and react-docgen run once each.\n\n### The budgets\n\nThe checker's whole-project run takes seconds and several hundred MiB to a GiB, so the 2 s and 600 MiB of the structural record no longer apply. No checker run of the five corpora has been measured: they are not installed where the change was made, and fetching them was not part of it. The reference for what to expect, from the fixtures of `docs/gate-measurements.md` (release build, default settings, macOS arm64, Apple M5 Max, shared machine at load 5 to 8, 3 interleaved runs, 2026-11-12):\n\n| Fixture | Components | Time | Peak RSS |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| `gate-large` | 938 | 5.80 to 6.35 s | 967 to 986 MiB |\n| Chakra wrappers alone | 787 | 5.22 to 5.41 s | 760 to 777 MiB |\n| three renamed copies of `gate-large` | 2,814 | 14.7 to 15.2 s | 1,046 to 1,050 MiB |\n\nWith the weekly's own settings (`--collapse-inherited-props none`, cache on) `gate-large` took 5.9 to 6.0 s and 1,025 to 1,077 MiB; the on-disk cache does not shorten the checker's pass. Time follows the size of the program the checker loads and memory hardly grows with the component count (one program, equal props interned). A GitHub `ubuntu-latest` runner is slower than that Mac and its RSS is not the same, and no CI run of the checker has been measured, so no ceiling is derived from these numbers for the corpora.\n\nThe rule that fills the budgets in, once a scheduled run has recorded the five corpora: take the larger of the first two scheduled runs, set the time budget to 1.5 times it and the peak-memory budget to 1.25 times it, rounded up to the next 0.5 s and 50 MiB, and write them in `BUDGETS` with the dates of the runs. The weekly, `agent_eval.py` and `bench.py` now run the default checker. I set no corpus budgets, because none could be measured. They are pushed on `feat/weekly-checker-default` as commit `26e8ca18d41857bc0199ab39d627075146807ec1`. `git ls-remote origin feat/weekly-checker-default` returns that same SHA.

**Branching:** the branch is stacked on `origin/feat/checker-is-default` at `0f71151a`. The PR is not opened and CI is not polled.

**Checks I ran, judged by exit code:**
- `just lint doc-check machete typos` exited 0. The first run failed on `oxfmt` formatting of `docs/measurement.md`; I formatted the file and it passed.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` exited 0 (138 tests, then re-run after the final edits).

**Code changes:**
- `--no-checker` is gone from every run in `scripts/weekly.py` (time/RSS, RDT-format components, layer members, oracle input), from `scripts/agent_eval.py` and from `scripts/bench.py`. Nothing else in `scripts` or `.github` still passes it; the only match left is a comment in `scripts/weekly.py`.
- I kept no structural reference row. The weekly never reported both resolvers, so there was nothing to preserve, and I added no options. The README claim of 34 to 81 ms is now described as measured by hand, with the weekly recording the default's time and memory.
- I bumped `UNIVERSE_VERSION` to 5 in `scripts/weekly.py`. Without that, the first checker record would be compared against last week's structural wrong-rate and could open a false "wrong types rose" issue. The summary now says the oracle's universe changed instead.

**Budgets, with the measurements behind them.** I built a release binary and ran three interleaved rounds on macOS arm64 (M5 Max, load 5 to 8, default settings, `--no-cache`, 2026-11-12). Raw output is in `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/weekly-checker/measure.log`.

| Fixture | Time | Peak RSS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gate-large` (938 components) | 5.80 to 6.35 s | 967 to 986 MiB |
| Chakra-only (787) | 5.22 to 5.41 s | 760 to 777 MiB |
| 3x `gate-large` (2,814) | 14.7 to 15.2 s | 1,046 to 1,050 MiB |

- **Matches S8:** these agree with your S8 figures.
- **Weekly settings:** `gate-large` with `--collapse-inherited-props none` and the cache on took 5.9 to 6.0 s and 1,025 to 1,077 MiB. The on-disk cache does not shorten the checker pass.
- **What I chose:** all five corpora (mantine, chakra, shadcn, antd, spectrum) have `{'ms': None, 'rss_mib': None}` in `BUDGETS` in `scripts/headline.py`. This is marked "record on first run" in code, docs and the summary text, and a run over a `None` opens no issue.
- **Why no ceiling from the fixtures:** GitHub ubuntu runners are slower than this Mac and their RSS differs, and no CI measurement of the checker exists. The fixtures also aren't the corpora. I did not invent a number from them.
- **Headroom rule, written into `docs/measurement.md` under a new "The budgets" section:** after the first two scheduled runs, take the larger of the two. Set time to 1.5 times it and peak memory to 1.25 times it, rounded up to the next 0.5 s and 50 MiB. The reason is that a shared runner drifts 10% or more on its own, plus pinned-commit growth.

**Docs changed:**
- `docs/measurement.md`: the weekly now records the checker, the new budgets section, the oracle paragraph and the issue-conditions bullet.
- `docs/gate-measurements.md`: one note under the S8 section.
- `docs/performance.md`, `docs/STATUS.md` (two places) and `docs/type-checker-integration.md`: reworded from "weekly is structural" to "weekly is the checker".
- `README.md`: the weekly-records sentence.

**Tests:** `scripts/test_headline.py` and `scripts/test_weekly_review.py` now patch `BUDGETS` for the over-budget cases. They add a test that every corpus budget is `None` and opens nothing, and a test for universe version 5. The old "largest corpus stays inside the budget" test is removed.

**Changeset:** none added. The earlier weekly fix, `47fdf0ed`, had none, and the changesets here are for packages.

**Not verified:**
- No checker run on the five weekly corpora (not installed, not fetched), so no corpus budget is derived.
- No `weekly.py --oracle`, no full weekly run, and no `bench.py` or `agent_eval.py` run.
- No Linux or CI run of the checker.
- The first scheduled run's table and summary are unseen. Its time, memory, recall and oracle numbers will all move, so the changes section will show large time and memory rises.
